rationale: Waydroid shares the host kernel and Linux does not provide an independent SELinux policy namespace for the Android container. The upstream integration therefore bypasses Android SELinux operations. This is a release risk requiring explicit acceptance; build-time neverallow enforcement alone does not mitigate it.
compensating_controls: Host LXC namespaces, cgroup device policy, seccomp and AppArmor confinement remain enabled and are verified on the shipping image.
Only the selected Etnaviv render node, allowlisted DMA heaps and capability-selected NXP decoder are exposed to Android.
Android application UID separation and non-root media services remain enabled; privileged debugging is disabled in production.
The container root filesystem is built from an immutable source lock and shipped with checksummed SBOM and build evidence.
The exception and upstream kernel/container isolation options are reviewed for every supported security release.
